items.action: Patch to OpenSSH 10.6p2 (or Alpine's updated packages) and restart sshd — the update alone is not enough. Audit Alpine-based container images and CI/CD pipelines.
items.details: The flaw traces to a 2016 patch for CVE-2016-6210 and affects OpenSSH on musl libc with PAM disabled, including Alpine's default server config. glibc-based distributions, Dropbear, and systems that check passwords through PAM are not affected. Fixed in OpenSSH 10.6p2.
items.summary: CVE-2026-123158 (CVSS 8.1), dubbed 'SSHole', lets an unauthenticated attacker log in to password-less accounts on OpenSSH running over musl libc — including Alpine Linux — with a single oversized password. Threat intel firm Previdian saw the first exploitation attempt under nine hours after disclosure and confirmed root access on a honeypot.
items.title: OpenSSH 'SSHole' auth bypass exploited within hours of disclosure

items.action: Apply Barracuda patches BNSF-40425 (9.4.017+) or BNSF-40430 (below 9.4.017) and keep ESG admin interfaces off the internet.
items.details: The bypass lives in the ESG's Index.pm handler, where a failed password change returns a valid role instead of halting the request. The command injection also affects five other Barracuda products, but there it still needs an admin account. ESG is fixed in firmware 9.4.0.030. Neither CVE is in CISA's KEV catalog and no in-the-wild exploitation has been reported.
items.summary: Two flaws in Barracuda's Email Security Gateway chain to unauthenticated root command execution: CVE-2026-116606 (CVSS 9.3), a pre-auth authorization bypass, and CVE-2026-111560 (CVSS 8.6), a command injection. watchTowr Labs published the full chain on Nov 5; Barracuda released patches on Nov 2.
items.title: Barracuda ESG flaws chained for root access without login

items.action: Install your distribution's fixed kernel and reboot. Prioritise internet-facing servers with MPTCP listeners.
items.details: Fixed kernels are already available from Red Hat, AlmaLinux, Debian and Amazon Linux; Ubuntu's fixes for 22.04, 24.04 and 26.04 LTS were still in testing as of Nov 6. Researchers have also seen residential proxies and Russia-based VPN servers scanning port 443 with MPTCP connections since Nov 2, though no vendor had reported attacks in the wild.
items.summary: A race condition leading to a use-after-free in the Linux kernel's IPv4 TCP handshake affects nearly every Linux distribution. Anthropic disclosed that an internal research version of its Claude model built a working exploit that runs commands as root against a server with a Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener.
items.title: Critical Linux kernel TCP flaw (CVE-2026-98432, CVSS 9.8)

items.action: Patch Gen7 and Gen8 SSL-VPN to the fixed releases and review which accounts can still sign in through alternate authentication methods.
items.details: Affects SSL-VPN configured for SAML on SonicOS Gen7 versions 7.3.3-7015 and earlier, and Gen8 versions 8.2.2-8015 and earlier. SonicWall's advisory is SNWLID-2026-0014. Known ransomware use is listed as unknown.
items.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-19868 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov 6. The SonicWall SonicOS SSL-VPN flaw lets a user with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method bypass SAML controls — including SAML-enforced MFA. Federal agencies must patch by Nov 20 under BOD 26-04.
items.title: CISA adds exploited SonicWall SSL-VPN flaw to KEV; patch by Nov 20

items.action: Chainalysis customers should rotate passwords and API keys as access returns, and watch for credential-stuffing and targeted phishing using the exposed identities.
items.details: The firm first disclosed the incident on Oct 30, initially saying no credentials were accessed. It still reports no evidence that investigation data was accessed or attribution data manipulated, and says the incident is unrelated to the recent Binance theft.
items.summary: Chainalysis widened its disclosure on Nov 4: names, usernames, password hashes and live tokens for all users were exposed to a malicious actor in an 'agentic' intrusion, and a separate on-path attack exposed a subset of customers' plaintext passwords. Reactor and Data Solutions remain offline; phased restoration of KYT and Address Screening began Nov 6.
items.title: Chainalysis breach widens: password hashes and live tokens for all users exposed

items.action: Centrepoint customers should watch for phishing using their loyalty details; retailers should review loyalty-program data exposure and third-party access.
items.details: The claim was discovered on Nov 6. The exposed data reportedly also includes shopper search sessions and per-query revenue intelligence. The claim is unverified by the retailer.
items.summary: The ransomware group N0n claims to have exfiltrated loyalty program records for 3,094,863 distinct customers of Saudi fashion retailer Centrepoint, including full names, email addresses, phone numbers and dates of birth. The data is listed as 'NOT PAID — EXPOSED' on the Ransomware.live tracker.
items.title: Ransomware group N0n claims 3.1M Centrepoint loyalty records

items.action: Advertisers and publishers in the Chartboost ecosystem should treat account and performance data as exposed and watch for fraud using the leaked pricing and earnings details.
items.details: The data is listed as 'NOT PAID — EXPOSED'. The archive spans January 2018 through September 2026 and includes impressions, clicks, installs, spend and earnings data, plus auction and bid pricing.
items.summary: Ransomware group N0n published a large archive stolen from mobile advertising network Chartboost on Nov 6, including publisher balance snapshots for 185,545 accounts, 1,129,048,884 performance rows covering 14,497 advertisers and 43,211 publishers, and a 293GB marketplace transaction archive.
items.title: N0n leaks massive Chartboost archive: 1.1B rows and a 293GB marketplace dump

items.action: Indian financial firms should treat AI-agent tooling as an active threat: tighten controls on payment and disbursement systems and staff monitoring through holidays and weekends.
items.details: The attackers use publicly available AI tools to automate break-ins 'at machine speed' and move money through victims' own payment and disbursement systems, timing attacks around holidays and weekends. Reuters previously reported two Mumbai-based non-bank lenders lost about $2 million in more than 700 unauthorised instant transfers from ICICI Bank accounts on Oct 8–9. CERT-In did not name the affected companies or say which incidents were linked to Crafty Falcon.
items.summary: CERT-In has named the hacking group 'Crafty Falcon' behind a wave of AI-driven attacks on Indian banks, non-bank lenders, fintech firms and crypto exchanges, calling the threat 'active and ongoing'. It named four AI tools the attackers use — ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI — at least two of them linked to China.
items.title: CERT-In names 'Crafty Falcon' behind AI-driven attacks on Indian financial firms

items.action: SBI customers should watch for targeted phishing and fraudulent loan applications using their KYC details; the bank says passwords and PINs are never asked for by its staff.
items.details: The exposed records reportedly included names, mobile numbers, email and residential addresses, dates of birth, gender, branch and CIF identifiers, lead IDs and metadata from loan or lead records. SBI learned of the exposure on Oct 16 from CERT-In, the Defence Cyber Agency and its threat-intelligence provider.
items.summary: State Bank of India is still evaluating the root cause of the recent breach that exposed personal data of 3,897 customers on the dark web, Chairman C. S. Setty said on Nov 3. The bank has run a cybersecurity drill including an API sweep and vulnerability assessments, with work ongoing.
items.title: SBI still probing cause of breach that exposed 3,897 customer records

subtitle: Saturday, November 7 — Here's what's worth your attention today.
title: Morning Cybersecurity Digest
